title: Finite-support monomial expansion in powers of a combined ideal
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings, $C:A\to B$ a unital ring homomorphism, $P$ an additive commutative monoid, and $z:P\to B$ a map with $z^0=1$ and $z^{p+q}=z^pz^q$. Let $J=(t_1,\ldots,t_h)$ be an ideal of $A$ generated by a finite list, allowing $h=0$, and let $\mathfrak b$ be the ideal of $B$ generated by $C(J)$ and all $z^q$ with $q\ne0$. For each integer $k\ge0$, $J^k$ consists exactly of finite $A$-linear combinations of the products $t_{j_1}\cdots t_{j_k}$; the product for $k=0$ is $1$, and for $h=0,k>0$ there are no such products and the only combination is zero. Let $S\subseteq P$ be finite, $n\ge1$, and for each $p\in S$ let $0\le l_p<n$ be an integer for which $p$ is a sum of $l_p$ nonzero elements of $P$, with the empty sum allowed. If $a_p\in J^{n-l_p}$ for every $p\in S$, then $\sum_{p\in S}C(a_p)z^p\in\mathfrak b^n$. More precisely, after choosing a decomposition $p=p_1+\cdots+p_{l_p}$ and an expression of $a_p$ as a finite sum of terms $c\,t_{j_1}\cdots t_{j_{n-l_p}}$, each summand $C(a_p)z^p$ is the corresponding finite sum of terms $C(c)C(t_{j_1})\cdots C(t_{j_{n-l_p}})z^{p_1}\cdots z^{p_{l_p}}$, each with exactly $n$ factors in $\mathfrak b$ after $C(c)$. An ideal power means the ideal of finite sums of products, with zeroth power the whole ring. The ideal-power convention is $J^0=A$ and $J^{k+1}=J^kJ$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring].

proof.text: Prove the generator assertion by induction on $k$, using $J^0=A$ and $J^{k+1}=J^kJ$ from [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring] and the statement's finite-product convention. At $k=0$, every $a\in A$ is $a\cdot1$. For the induction step, an element of $J^kJ$ is a finite sum of $xy$ with $x\in J^k$ and $y\in J$. Write $x=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha\prod_{r=1}^k t_{j_{\alpha,r}}$ by induction and $y=\sum_{j=1}^h d_jt_j$ by the meaning of $J=(t_1,\ldots,t_h)$. Distributing gives terms $c_\alpha d_j(\prod_{r=1}^k t_{j_{\alpha,r}})t_j$, of the required length $k+1$. Conversely every such product has its first $k$ factors in $J^k$ and last factor in $J$, hence lies in $J^{k+1}$; scalar multiples and finite sums remain there. If $h=0$, $J=0$, and at every positive degree the expansion is empty and equals zero.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: formal monoid models; elementary agent-supplied finite coefficient argument, not a theorem asserted in ILO.

proof.text:
Fix $p\in S$ and its chosen decomposition $p=p_1+\cdots+p_{l_p}$. Put $k=n-l_p$. Step 1 provides a finite expression $a_p=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha\prod_{r=1}^k t_{j_{\alpha,r}}$. Iterating $z^{u+v}=z^uz^v$ gives $z^p=\prod_{s=1}^{l_p}z^{p_s}$, including $l_p=0$ by $z^0=1$. Since $C$ preserves addition, multiplication and $1$, finite distributivity gives
$$C(a_p)z^p=\sum_\alpha C(c_\alpha)\left(\prod_{r=1}^k C(t_{j_{\alpha,r}})\right)\left(\prod_{s=1}^{l_p}z^{p_s}\right).$$
This is the specified expansion for any choices of the coefficient expression and decomposition.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: formal monoid models; elementary agent-supplied finite coefficient argument, not a theorem asserted in ILO.

proof.text: Every $t_j$ belongs to $J$, so $C(t_j)\in\mathfrak b$ by its generating set. Also $z^{p_s}\in\mathfrak b$ because each $p_s\ne0$. Thus each term in step 2 after $C(c_\alpha)$ is a product of $k+l_p=(n-l_p)+l_p=n$ elements of $\mathfrak b$. By the finite-product convention it lies in $\mathfrak b^n$, and multiplication by $C(c_\alpha)$ preserves this ideal. Closure under the finite sum over $\alpha$ proves $C(a_p)z^p\in\mathfrak b^n$. Closure under the finite sum over $p\in S$ proves the conclusion. Empty sums are zero, so this also covers $S=\varnothing$ and, since $k>0$, the empty generator list.

lean.statement: theorem finite_support_monomial_ideal_power (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (B : Type v) [CommRing B] (C : A →+* B) (P : Type w) [AddCommMonoid P] (z : P → B) (hz0 : z 0 = 1) (hzadd : ∀ p q : P, z (p + q) = z p * z q) (h : ℕ) (t : Fin h → A) (J : Ideal A) (hJ : J = Ideal.span (Set.range t)) (b : Ideal B) (hb : b = Ideal.span (C '' (J : Set A) ∪ z '' {q : P | q ≠ 0})) : (∀ (k : ℕ) (a : A), a ∈ J ^ k ↔ ∃ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin m → A) (j : Fin m → Fin k → Fin h), a = ∑ α : Fin m, c α * ∏ r : Fin k, t (j α r)) ∧ (∀ (S : Finset P) (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (l : P → ℕ) (a : P → A), (∀ p ∈ S, l p < n) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∃ d : Fin (l p) → P, (∀ s : Fin (l p), d s ≠ 0) ∧ (∑ s : Fin (l p), d s) = p) → (∀ p ∈ S, a p ∈ J ^ (n - l p)) → (∑ p ∈ S, C (a p) * z p) ∈ b ^ n ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, C (a p) * z p ∈ b ^ n ∧ ∀ d : Fin (l p) → P, (∀ s : Fin (l p), d s ≠ 0) → (∑ s : Fin (l p), d s) = p → ∀ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin m → A) (j : Fin m → Fin (n - l p) → Fin h), a p = (∑ α : Fin m, c α * ∏ r : Fin (n - l p), t (j α r)) → C (a p) * z p = (∑ α : Fin m, C (c α) * (∏ r : Fin (n - l p), C (t (j α r))) * (∏ s : Fin (l p), z (d s))) ∧ (n - l p) + l p = n ∧ (∀ (α : Fin m) (r : Fin (n - l p)), C (t (j α r)) ∈ b) ∧ (∀ s : Fin (l p), z (d s) ∈ b) ∧ (∀ α : Fin m, C (c α) * (∏ r : Fin (n - l p), C (t (j α r))) * (∏ s : Fin (l p), z (d s)) ∈ b ^ n))
